correctness.rationale: The mixed derivative is exactly 1+a xy+bP2(x)P2(y); marginal integrals vanish. Density positivity forces -1<=b<=2 and reduces to the exact infimum of [1+bP2(s)P2(t)]/(st). At fixed w=st, R=s/t+t/s ranges between 2 and w+1/w; monotonicity in R gives q_-(w) and q_+(w). Their global minimization yields H(b) in three regimes, with endpoints included and concrete negative-density witnesses beyond each boundary. Two independent definitions of Kendall tau agree, and direct rational integration proves rho=lambda1 and tau=(2lambda1/3)(1+lambda2/5). Global rank maxima follow by a one-variable derivative with unique critical root sqrt(171). The standard-library verifier passed six exact algebraic nodes, four exact normalization cases, and 33371 finite numerical probes; continuum proof is analytic.

originality.rationale: The original 2023 model, 2024 publication, and 2025 estimation follow-up provide only sufficient coefficient regions. Those implications are strictly weaker than an exact if-and-only-if curved feasible set, and their bounded lambda1<=1/3 examples do not contain the now-explicit lambda1=1/sqrt(3) feasible extremizer. Closely related later multivariate and 1-dependent articles have non-dominating coefficient domains or different kernels. Comparison with published mathematical records, alias/parameter searches, source equations and accessible full-text sections disclosed no equivalent theorem. Residual possibility of an unindexed equivalent positivity computation remains acknowledged.

value.rationale: A complete admissibility region is a natural structural property of a named two-mode copula used for dependence modeling and parameter estimation. The nonlinear boundary supplies valid coefficients excluded by both previously stated sufficient regions, extends the exact attainable Spearman magnitude from 1/3 to 1/sqrt(3), and gives a distinct sharp Kendall extremizer at the algebraic b*=(sqrt171-11)/2. The result explains the true model parameter space, not an arbitrary slice or a mere computation; it does not claim general multivariate, mixing, or statistical efficiency consequences.
